en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammānuloma (1), Tikapaṭṭhānapāḷi (1) 1.1.
Nikkhepavāra (The Section on the Exposition)
Homage to that Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Self-Awakened One.
1.1.1. Summary of Conditions:
The root condition, the object condition, the predominance condition, the proximity condition, the contiguity condition.
Co-nascence condition, mutuality condition, support condition, decisive support condition, prenascence condition,
postnascence condition, repetition condition, kamma condition, resultant condition, nutriment condition, faculty condition, jhāna condition, path condition,
association condition, dissociation condition, presence condition, absence condition.
"Condition that has disappeared" (*vigatapaccaya*) and "condition that has not disappeared" (*avigatapaccaya*).
This is the enumeration of conditions (*paccayuddesa*). 1.1.2. Exposition of Conditions (*paccayaniddesa*).
Root condition (*hetupaccaya*): Roots are a condition, by way of root condition, for the states associated with the roots and for the material phenomena originated by them.
Object condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*): The visible-object base is a condition, by way of object condition, for the eye-consciousness element and for the states associated with it.
The sound-base is a condition... for the ear-consciousness element and for the states associated with it.

It is a condition by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*). The odor-base (*gandhāyatana*) is a condition by way of object-condition for the nose-consciousness-element (*ghānaviññāṇadhātu*) and for the states associated with it.
The taste-base (*rasāyatana*) is a condition by way of object-condition for the tongue-consciousness-element (*jivhāviññāṇadhātu*) and for the states associated with it.
The tangible-base (*phoṭṭhabbāyatana*) [is a condition] for the body-consciousness-element (*kāyaviññāṇadhātu*) and for the states associated with it...

Phenomena are related to phenomena by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*). The visible-object base, sound-base, odor-base, flavor-base, and tangible-object base are related to the mind-element (*manodhātu*) and its associated states by way of object-condition.
All phenomena are related to the mind-consciousness-element (*manoviññāṇadhātu*) and its associated states by way of object-condition.

Whatever states, whether consciousness or mental factors, arise contingent upon whatever state, those [latter] states are a condition for those [former] states by way of the object-condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*).

As for the predominance-condition (*adhipati-paccaya*): the predominance of desire (*chanda-adhipati*) is a condition by way of the predominance-condition for those states associated with desire and for the material phenomena originated thereby. The predominance of energy (*viriya-adhipati*) [is a condition] for those states associated with energy...
And it is a condition by way of predominance-condition for the material phenomena produced thereby.

Mental predominance is a condition by way of predominance-condition for states associated with consciousness and for the material phenomena produced thereby. Investigative predominance is a condition by way of predominance-condition for states associated with investigation and for the material phenomena produced thereby.

Whatever states, whether mental or mental concomitants, arise by taking certain other states as estimable (garu), those [latter] states are related to those [former] states by way of the predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya*).

As for the proximity condition (*anantarapaccaya*): the eye-consciousness element and its associated states are related to the mind-element and its associated states by way of the proximity condition; and the mind-element and its associated states [are related] to the mind-consciousness element...
And it is a condition for its associated states by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*).
The ear-consciousness element and its associated states are a condition for the mind-element (*manodhātu*) and its associated states by way of proximity-condition.
The mind-element and its associated states [are a condition] for the mind-consciousness element...
And it is a condition for its associated states by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*).
The nose-consciousness-element and its associated states are a condition for the mind-element and its associated states by way of proximity-condition.
The mind-element and its associated states [are a condition] for the mind-consciousness-element...
And it is a condition for its associated states by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*).
The tongue-consciousness element and its associated states are a condition for the mind-element and its associated states by way of proximity-condition.
The mind-element and its associated states [are a condition] for the mind-consciousness element...
And it is a condition for its associated states by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*).
The body-consciousness element and its associated states are a condition for the mind-element and its associated states by way of proximity-condition.
The mind-element and its associated states [are a condition] for the mind-consciousness element...
And it is a condition for the states associated with it by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*).
Previous wholesome states are a condition for subsequent wholesome states by way of proximity-condition.
Previous wholesome states are [a condition] for subsequent indeterminate states by way of proximity-condition.
Condition by way of proximity condition (*anantarapaccaya*).
Preceding unwholesome states are a condition for subsequent unwholesome states by way of proximity condition.
Preceding unwholesome states are a condition for subsequent indeterminate states by way of proximity condition.
It is a condition by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*).
Preceding indeterminate states (*abyākata-dhamma*) are a condition for subsequent indeterminate states by way of proximity-condition.
Preceding indeterminate states are [also a condition] for subsequent wholesome states (*kusala-dhamma*).
It is a condition by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*). Preceding indeterminate states are a condition for subsequent unwholesome states by way of proximity-condition.
Whatever states, whether mental or mental concomitants, arise immediately after whatever states, those [preceding] states are a condition for those [subsequent] states by way of proximity-condition.

Proximity condition (*samanantarapaccaya*): The eye-consciousness element and the states associated with it are a condition for the mind-element and the states associated with it by way of proximity condition.
The mind-element and the states associated with it are a condition for the mind-consciousness element and the states associated with it by way of proximity condition.
The ear-consciousness element and the states associated with it are a condition for the mind-element and the states associated with it by way of proximity-condition (*samanantara-paccaya*).
The mind-element and the states associated with it are a condition for the mind-consciousness element and the states associated with it by way of proximity-condition.

The nose-consciousness element and the states associated with it are related to the mind-element and the states associated with it by way of the condition of immediate antecedence (*samanantara-paccaya*). The mind-element and the states associated with it are related to the mind-consciousness element and the states associated with it by way of the condition of immediate antecedence.
The tongue-consciousness element and the states associated with it are a condition for the mind-element and the states associated with it by way of proximity-condition (*samanantara-paccaya*).
The mind-element and the states associated with it are a condition for the mind-consciousness element and the states associated with it by way of proximity-condition.

The body-consciousness element and the states associated with it are a condition for the mind-element and the states associated with it by way of the immediately preceding condition (*samanantara-paccaya*). The mind-element and the states associated with it are a condition for the mind-consciousness element and the states associated with it by way of the immediately preceding condition.
Preceding wholesome states are a condition for succeeding wholesome states by way of the condition of immediate succession.
Preceding wholesome states are a condition for succeeding indeterminate states by way of the condition of immediate succession.
Preceding unwholesome states are a condition for subsequent unwholesome states by way of proximity-condition (*samanantara-paccaya*).
Preceding unwholesome states are a condition for subsequent indeterminate states by way of proximity-condition.
Preceding indeterminate states are a condition for subsequent indeterminate states by way of the condition of immediate succession (*samanantara-paccaya*).
Preceding indeterminate states are a condition for subsequent wholesome states by way of the condition of immediate succession. Preceding indeterminate states are [a condition] for subsequent...
It is a condition for unwholesome states by way of the proximity-condition (*samanantara-paccaya*).

Whatever states, whether consciousness or mental factors, arise immediately after whatever [preceding] states, those [subsequent] states are a condition for those [preceding] states by way of the proximity-condition.
As for the co-nascence-condition (*sahajāta-paccaya*): the four immaterial aggregates are a condition for one another by way of the co-nascence-condition. The four...

The great elements (mahābhūta) are related to one another by way of the condition of co-nascence (sahajātapaccaya). At the moment of conception (okkantikkhaṇa), name-and-form (nāmarūpa) are related to one another by way of the condition of co-nascence.
Mental states and mental factors (cittacetasika-dhamma) are related to mind-produced matter (cittasamuṭṭhāna-rūpa) by way of the condition of co-nascence.
The great elements are related to derived matter (upādārūpa) by way of the condition of co-nascence. Material phenomena (rūpino dhammā) [are related] to immaterial phenomena...
Regarding phenomena (*dhammā*): at some times they are a condition by way of co-nascence condition (*sahajāta-paccaya*), and at other times they are not a condition by way of co-nascence condition.

As for the mutuality condition (*aññamañña-paccaya*): the four formless aggregates (*arūpino khandhā*) are a condition by way of mutuality condition; the four great elements (*mahābhūtā*) are a condition by way of mutuality condition; at the moment of conception (*okkantikkhaṇe*), name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*) is a condition by way of mutuality condition.
As for the support condition (*nissaya-paccaya*): the four formless aggregates are a condition for one another by way of support condition. The four...
The great elements are related to one another by way of the condition of support. At the moment of conception, name-and-form are related to one another by way of the condition of support.
Mental states and mental factors are related to mind-originated material phenomena by way of the condition of support.
The great elements are related to derived material phenomena by way of the condition of support.
The eye-base is a condition, by way of support-condition, for the eye-consciousness element and for the states associated with it.
The ear-base is a condition, by way of support-condition, for the ear-consciousness element and for the states associated with it.
The nose-base is a condition, by way of support-condition, for the nose-consciousness element and for the states associated with it.
Condition: The tongue-base is a condition, by way of support-condition, for the tongue-consciousness-element and for the states associated with it.
The body-base is a condition, by way of support-condition, for the body-consciousness-element and for the states associated with it.
Whatever material form depending upon which the mind-element and the mind-consciousness-element proceed—that material form is [a condition] for the mind-element...
And the mind-consciousness element and the mental states associated with it are related to each other by way of the support-condition (*nissaya-paccaya*).

As for the decisive-support-condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*): preceding wholesome states are related to succeeding wholesome states by way of the decisive-support-condition. Preceding wholesome states [are related] to succeeding wholesome states...
Certain unwholesome states are related to [other] unwholesome states by way of the decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).
Previous wholesome states are related to subsequent indeterminate states by way of the decisive support condition.
Previous unwholesome states are related to subsequent unwholesome states by way of the decisive support condition.

Condition: Previous unwholesome states are a condition for subsequent wholesome states by way of decisive support condition (upanissaya-paccaya). Previous unwholesome states are a condition for subsequent indeterminate states by way of decisive support condition.
Preceding indeterminate states are a condition for subsequent indeterminate states by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).
Preceding indeterminate states are a condition for subsequent wholesome states by way of decisive support condition. Preceding indeterminate states [are a condition] for subsequent...
It is a condition for unwholesome states by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

Weather and food are also conditions by way of decisive support condition. A person is also a condition by way of decisive support condition. Lodgings are also a condition by way of decisive support condition. As for the "prenascence condition" (*purejāta-paccaya*):
the eye-base is a condition for the eye-consciousness element and for the states associated with it.
It is a condition by way of prenascence condition. The ear-base is a condition by way of prenascence condition for the ear-consciousness-element and for the states associated with it.
The nose-base is a condition by way of prenascence condition for the nose-consciousness-element and for the states associated with it.
The tongue-base is a condition by way of prenascence condition for the tongue-consciousness-element and for the states associated with it... [and so forth].

It is a condition for mental phenomena by way of the prenascence condition. The body-base is a condition for the body-consciousness element and the phenomena associated with it by way of the prenascence condition.
The visible-form base is a condition for the eye-consciousness element and the phenomena associated with it by way of the prenascence condition.
Condition: The sound-base is a pre-arising condition for the ear-consciousness-element and for the states associated with it.
The odor-base is a pre-arising condition for the nose-consciousness-element and for the states associated with it.
The taste-base is a pre-arising condition for the tongue-consciousness-element and for the states associated with it.
The tangible object base is a pre-arising condition for the body-consciousness element and for the states associated with it.
The visible object base, sound base, odor base, taste base, and tangible object base are pre-arising conditions for the mind-element and for the states associated with it.

That material form depending upon which the mind-element (*manodhātu*) and the mind-consciousness-element (*manoviññāṇadhātu*) proceed is a condition for the mind-element and for the states associated with it by way of pre-nascence condition (*purejātapaccaya*). For the mind-consciousness-element and for the states associated with it,
it is at times a condition by way of pre-nascence condition, and at other times not a condition by way of pre-nascence condition.
Postnascence condition (*pacchājāta-paccaya*): Mind and mental factors that have arisen later are a condition by way of postnascence for this body that has arisen earlier.

Habitual repetition condition (*āsevana-paccaya*): Preceding wholesome states are a condition by way of habitual repetition for succeeding wholesome states; preceding unwholesome states [are a condition] for succeeding unwholesome states...

States are related to states by way of the condition of repetition. Previous functional-ineffective states are related to subsequent functional-ineffective states by way of the condition of repetition.
As for the condition of kamma: wholesome and unwholesome kamma is related to resultant aggregates and to the matter produced by kamma by way of the condition of kamma.
Condition: Volition is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for associated states and for the material phenomena originated by them.
Resultant-condition: The four immaterial resultant aggregates are a condition, by way of resultant-condition, for one another.

Nutriment-condition: Edible food is a condition, by way of nutriment-condition, for this body. The immaterial nutriments are a condition, by way of nutriment-condition, for associated states and for the material phenomena originated by them.
Condition by faculty: the eye-faculty is a condition, by way of the faculty-condition, for the eye-consciousness element and for the states associated with it.
The ear-faculty is a condition, by way of the faculty-condition, for the ear-consciousness element and for the states associated with it.
The nose-faculty is a condition, by way of the faculty-condition, for the nose-consciousness element and for the states associated with it... [and so forth].
Condition by way of faculty condition: The tongue-faculty is a condition by way of faculty condition for tongue-consciousness-element and for the states associated with it.
The body-faculty is a condition by way of faculty condition for body-consciousness-element and for the states associated with it.
The material life-faculty is a condition by way of faculty condition for the types of matter produced by kamma.
The immaterial faculties are related to their associated states and to the material phenomena originated by them by way of faculty condition (*indriya-paccaya*).
As for the jhāna condition (*jhāna-paccaya*): the factors of jhāna are related to the states associated with jhāna and to the material phenomena originated by them by way of jhāna condition.
As for the path condition (*magga-paccaya*): the factors of the path are related to the states associated with the path and to the material phenomena originated by them by way of path condition.
Association-condition (*sampayutta-paccaya*): The four formless aggregates (*arūpa-khandha*) are mutually related to one another by way of the association-condition.

Dissociation-condition (*vippayutta-paccaya*): Material phenomena (*rūpa-dhamma*) are related to immaterial phenomena (*arūpa-dhamma*) by way of the dissociation-condition; immaterial phenomena are related to material phenomena by way of the dissociation-condition. Presence-condition (*atthi-paccaya*):
The four formless aggregates are mutually related to one another by way of the presence-condition. The four...

The great primary elements (mahābhūta) are related to one another by way of presence condition (atthipaccaya). At the moment of conception, name-and-form (nāmarūpa) are related to one another by way of presence condition.
Mental states and mental factors (cittacetasika-dhamma) are related to mind-produced matter (cittasamuṭṭhāna-rūpa) by way of presence condition.
The great primary elements are related to derived matter (upādārūpa) by way of presence condition.
The eye-base is a condition, by way of presence-condition, for the eye-consciousness element and for the states associated with it.
The ear-base is a condition, by way of presence-condition, for the ear-consciousness element and for the states associated with it.
The nose-base is a condition, by way of presence-condition, for the nose-consciousness element and for the states associated with it.
Condition: The tongue-base is a presence condition for the tongue-consciousness-element and for the states associated with it.
The body-base is a presence condition for the body-consciousness-element and for the states associated with it.
The visible-form base is a presence condition for the eye-consciousness-element and for the states associated with it.
The sense-base of sound is a condition, by way of presence-condition, for the ear-consciousness-element and for the mental states associated with it.
The sense-base of odor is a condition, by way of presence-condition, for the nose-consciousness-element and for the mental states associated with it.
The sense-base of flavor is a condition, by way of presence-condition, for the tongue-consciousness-element and for the mental states associated with it.
The tangible object base is a condition, by way of presence-condition, for body-consciousness-element and for those states associated with it.
The visible-object base, sound-base, odor-base, taste-base, and tangible-object base are conditions,
by way of presence-condition, for mind-element and for those states associated with it.

That material form depending upon which the mind-element (*manodhātu*) and the mind-consciousness-element (*manoviññāṇadhātu*) proceed is a condition for the mind-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and the mental states associated with them, by way of presence-condition (*atthipaccaya*). As for non-existence-condition (*natthipaccaya*):
mental states consisting of consciousness and mental factors that have ceased immediately prior are a condition for present consciousness and mental factors by way of non-existence-condition.

"Condition by disappearance" (*vigatapaccaya*): Immediately preceding mental states and mental factors (*cittacetasika*) that have disappeared are a condition by way of condition by disappearance for present mental states and mental factors.
"Condition by non-disappearance" (*avigatapaccaya*): The four formless aggregates (*arūpakkhandha*) are mutually a condition by way of condition by non-disappearance.

The four great elements (*mahābhūta*) are mutually a condition by way of condition by non-disappearance. At the moment of conception (*okkantikkhaṇe*), mentality and materiality (*nāmarūpa*) are mutually [a condition by way of condition by non-disappearance].
Condition by way of non-disappearance condition: mental states and mental factors are a condition for mind-produced matter by way of non-disappearance condition;
the great primary elements are a condition for derived matter by way of non-disappearance condition;
the eye-base is a condition for the eye-consciousness element and its associated states by way of non-disappearance condition.
Condition: The ear-base is a condition, by way of non-disappearance condition, for the ear-consciousness element and for the states associated with it.
The nose-base is a condition, by way of non-disappearance condition, for the nose-consciousness element and for the states associated with it.
The tongue-base is a condition, by way of non-disappearance condition, for the tongue-consciousness element and for the states associated with it.
Condition: The body-base is a condition, by way of non-disappearance condition, for the body-consciousness element and for the states associated with it.
The visible-form base is a condition, by way of non-disappearance condition, for the eye-consciousness element and for the states associated with it.
The sound-base is a condition, by way of non-disappearance condition, for the ear-consciousness element and for the states associated with it.
Condition: The odor-base is a condition, by way of non-disappearance condition, for the nose-consciousness element and for the states associated with it.
The taste-base is a condition, by way of non-disappearance condition, for the tongue-consciousness element and for the states associated with it.
The tangible-base is a condition, by way of non-disappearance condition, for the body-consciousness element and for the states associated with it.
Condition: The visible-object base, sound-base, odor-base, taste-base, and tangible-object base are related to the mind-element and its associated states by way of non-disappearance condition.

Whatever material form depending upon which the mind-element and the mind-consciousness-element proceed, that material form is related to the mind-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and their associated states by way of non-disappearance condition.
Exposition of Conditions. 1.1.3.
Section on Questions. 1.1.3.1.
Positive Order of Conditions.
Wholesome Section It may be that, dependent on a wholesome state, a wholesome state arises by way of the root condition. It may be that, dependent on a wholesome state...
Dependent on a wholesome state, an unwholesome state might arise by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a wholesome state, an indeterminate state might arise by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a wholesome state, both wholesome and indeterminate states might arise by way of the root condition. Dependent on a wholesome state, both unwholesome and indeterminate...
And states may arise conditioned by a wholesome state through the condition of root.

It may be that, dependent on a wholesome state, both wholesome and unwholesome states arise through the condition of root. It may be that, dependent on a wholesome state, wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate states arise through the condition of root.
1.3.1.1.2. Unwholesome Section (Akusalapada) It may be that, dependent on an unwholesome state, an unwholesome state arises by way of root condition.
It may be that, dependent on an unwholesome state, a wholesome state arises by way of root condition. It may be that, dependent on an unwholesome state...
An indeterminate state might arise by way of the root condition. It may be that, dependent on an unwholesome state, both wholesome and indeterminate states arise by way of the root condition.

It may be that, dependent on an unwholesome state, both unwholesome and indeterminate states arise by way of the root condition. It may be that, dependent on an unwholesome state, both wholesome and unwholesome...
And states may arise conditioned by a root-condition. It may be that, dependent on an unwholesome state, wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate states may arise conditioned by a root-condition.
1.3.1.1.3. Indeterminate Section.
It may be that, dependent on an indeterminate state, an indeterminate state arises by way of the root-condition.
It may be that, dependent on an indeterminate state, a wholesome state arises by way of the root-condition.

It may be that, dependent on an indeterminate state, an unwholesome state arises by way of the root-condition. It may be that, dependent on an indeterminate state, both a wholesome and an indeterminate [state arise]...
And states may arise conditioned by a cause. It may be that, dependent on an indeterminate state, unwholesome and indeterminate states arise conditioned by a cause.
It may be that, dependent on an indeterminate state, wholesome and unwholesome states arise conditioned by a cause. It may be that, dependent on an indeterminate state, wholesome and unwholesome...
And indeterminate states may arise by way of the root condition.
1.3.1.1.4. The Section on the Wholesome and Indeterminate:
It may be that, dependent upon both wholesome and indeterminate states, a wholesome state arises by way of the root condition.
It may be that, dependent on wholesome and indeterminate states, an unwholesome state arises by way of the root-condition (hetupaccaya).
It may be that, dependent on wholesome and indeterminate states, an indeterminate state arises by way of the root-condition.
It may be that, dependent on wholesome and indeterminate states, both wholesome and indeterminate states arise.
By way of root condition. It may be that, dependent on a wholesome and indeterminate state, unwholesome and indeterminate states arise by way of root condition.

It may be that, dependent on a wholesome and indeterminate state, wholesome and unwholesome states arise by way of root condition. It may be that, dependent on a wholesome and indeterminate state, a wholesome...
And unwholesome and indeterminate states might arise by way of the root condition.
1.3.1.1.5. The Section on the Unwholesome and Indeterminate:
It may be that, dependent upon both unwholesome and indeterminate states, a wholesome state arises by way of the root condition.
It may be that, dependent on unwholesome and indeterminate states, an unwholesome state arises by way of the root-condition.
It may be that, dependent on unwholesome and indeterminate states, an indeterminate state arises by way of the root-condition.
It may be that, dependent on unwholesome and indeterminate states, both wholesome and indeterminate states arise.
By way of root condition (*hetupaccaya*). It may be that, dependent on unwholesome and indeterminate states, unwholesome and indeterminate states arise by way of root condition.

It may be that, dependent on unwholesome and indeterminate states, wholesome and unwholesome states arise by way of root condition. It may be that, dependent on unwholesome and indeterminate states, wholesome...
And unwholesome and indeterminate states might arise by way of the root condition.
1.3.1.1.6. The Section on the Wholesome and Unwholesome:
It may be that, dependent upon both wholesome and unwholesome states, a wholesome state arises by way of the root condition. It may be...
Dependent on both wholesome and unwholesome states, an unwholesome state may arise by way of the root condition.
Dependent on both wholesome and unwholesome states, an indeterminate state may arise by way of the root condition.
Dependent on both wholesome and unwholesome states, both wholesome and indeterminate states may arise by way of the root condition.
It may be that, dependent on both wholesome and unwholesome states, unwholesome and indeterminate states arise by way of the root condition.

It may be that, dependent on both wholesome and unwholesome states, wholesome and unwholesome states arise by way of the root condition. It may be that, dependent on both wholesome and unwholesome states, wholesome and unwholesome...
And indeterminate states might arise by way of the root condition.
1.3.1.1.7. The Section on Wholesome, Unwholesome, and Indeterminate States:
It may be that, dependent upon a wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate state, a wholesome state arises by way of the root condition.
It may be that, dependent on a wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate state, an unwholesome state arises by way of the root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*).

It may be that, dependent on a wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate state, an indeterminate state arises by way of the root-condition. It may be that, dependent on a wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate state, a wholesome and indeterminate [state arises].

And [it may be that] states arise with a root-condition. It may be that, dependent on a state that is wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate, there arise states that are unwholesome and indeterminate with a root-condition.
It may be that, dependent on a state that is wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate, there arise states that are wholesome and unwholesome with a root-condition.
It may be that, dependent on a state that is wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate, there arise states that are wholesome, unwholesome,
and indeterminate by way of root-condition. This is the section on the root-condition.
It may be that, dependent on a wholesome state, a wholesome state arises by way of the object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*).
(Just as the root-condition was explained in detail, so too should the object-condition be explained in full according to the recitation method.
It may be that, dependent on a wholesome state, a wholesome state arises by way of the predominance-condition (*adhipatipaccaya*) … the proximity-condition (*anantarapaccaya*).

… by way of immediate condition … by way of conascence condition … by way of mutuality condition … by way of support condition … by way of decisive support condition … by way of prenascence condition … by way of postnascence condition … by way of repetition condition … by way of kamma condition … by way of resultant condition … by way of nutriment condition … by way of faculty condition … by way of jhāna condition … by way of path condition … by way of association condition …
… by dissociation-condition … by presence-condition … by absence-condition … by disappearance-condition.
